StorySheet

User Guide — A step-by-step tour of creating, editing, designing, adding music, previewing, and sharing your story.

Draft for review: Based on six supplied screen recordings. This guide documents demonstrated workflows; unpublished or unshown features have not been assumed.
1. Start a StorySheet2. Arrange and manage moments3. Add captions, stickers, and filters4. Mark up a photo5. Choose a page layout6. Add picture borders7. Add music you have permission to use8. Preview and save your StorySheet9. Create a video preview10. Share a WebShare link

1. Start a StorySheet

Your Story
  1. Open the Your Story tab. Expand Add a title, enter your story name, and adjust the Creation Date if needed.
  2. Optionally tap Add Header Logo. Under Your moments, tap Add a moment or the blue plus button.
  3. Choose photos from the photo picker, select your images, and confirm. Your chosen moments appear as numbered thumbnails.

From the recording: A title and date were entered for a sample visit to a brewery.

2. Arrange and manage moments

Your Story
  1. From the moments list, tap a photo thumbnail to open its editing tools.
  2. Use Reorder to open the Reorder Photos list. Drag the handles to change the sequence, then tap Done.
  3. Use the red X on an individual thumbnail to remove it from the project.

From the recording: The recording demonstrates the Reorder Photos drag handles and a grid of selected moments, including a video.

3. Add captions, stickers, and filters

Your Story
  1. Tap an image in Your moments. Use Captions to enter a description, then tap Done.
  2. Use Stickers, browse or search the available designs, and place a sticker on the image.
  3. Use Filters to preview looks for a photo and choose the result you want.

From the recording: The recordings demonstrate a photo caption, a ghost sticker, and a sepia-style filter preview.

4. Mark up a photo

Your Story
  1. Open a photo and choose Mark-up.
  2. In Draw mode, select Arrow, Circle, Rectangle, or Highlight as needed.
  3. Use the drawing tools on your photo, review the changes, and tap Done when finished.

From the recording: The recording shows red arrow and rectangle annotations.

5. Choose a page layout

Design
  1. Tap Design in the bottom navigation. Browse the live preview; use the arrows to move between pages or tap it to enlarge.
  2. Under Page layout, choose Photo grid or Full size - no background.
  3. For Photo grid, select the number of photos per page. The screen shows choices of 1, 2, 4, 9, 16, or 36 per page.

From the recording: The preview shows page counts and adjusts when layout options change.

6. Add picture borders

Design
  1. Scroll to Borders on the Design screen.
  2. Choose the desired border. The recording shows None, Polaroid, Notebook, Scrapbook, and Classic.
  3. Review the effect in the live preview before sharing or exporting.

From the recording: Borders are presented as a finishing touch around each photo.

7. Add music you have permission to use

Preview & Share
  1. Under Background Music, tap Add Background Music.
  2. Read the Music Rights notice. Only use music you own or have permission to use, then confirm your rights.
  3. Use Import Music to choose an audio file from Files. The app lists MP3, M4A, WAV, and AIFF as supported formats.

From the recording: The app states that music mixes into MP4 videos; PDFs and Photo Sheets stay unchanged. It lowers during clips with speech.

8. Preview and save your StorySheet

Preview & Share
  1. Tap Preview & Share. On the Photo Sheet tab, move through the pages and tap to enlarge a page.
  2. Scroll to the available output choices: Print, Save PDF only, and Save complete story.
  3. The app describes Save complete story as PDF + videos + guide for offline keeping and watching.

From the recording: The export screen notes that tapping a video cover inside an exported PDF requires internet access, and video links may be available for up to 7 days.

9. Create a video preview

Preview & Share
  1. On Preview & Share, choose the WebShare or video-preview area shown in the recording.
  2. Tap Create Preview if no video preview is available. Wait while the app creates it.
  3. When finished, play the preview or use the scrubber to move through the video.

From the recording: The example shows a generated video preview with playback controls.

10. Share a WebShare link

Preview & Share
  1. On the WebShare tab, choose Play or Scroll presentation style.
  2. Tap Create WebShare Link and wait for uploading to finish.
  3. Use the iOS share sheet to copy the link or send it through an available sharing app.

From the recording: The recording demonstrates sharing a link and opening a finished story in a browser. Be mindful that online sharing involves uploading.

Important notes

Music rights: Use only music you own or are permitted to use. StorySheet asks you to confirm your rights before importing.

Online vs offline: The app states PDF video links require internet access and can expire after up to seven days. “Save complete story” includes PDF, videos, and a guide for offline use.

Not yet demonstrated: TikTok posting steps, detailed background selection, video trimming, and all settings. We can add these after reviewing additional recordings.
